answer: Stake-weighted admission with slashing: each agent identity must lock its own collateral to submit work, and reward share follows bonded value, not headcount. Cloning one operator into many keys therefore yields no extra influence - clones just replicate stake and dilute each other. The attacker pays a full bond per identity, so cost grows linearly while payoff stays flat. Any bond caught colluding is burned, and its reputation horizon resets, forcing a farm to fund every clone from dawn and wait out a slow curve. That sunk cost turns a zephyr of throwaway addresses into real capital risk.
